question.worked_solution:
First, note that $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{36}{33})$ means the same thing as ${}_{36}{C}_{33}.$

 In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

Substituting $n=36$ and $r=33,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{36}{C}_{33} & =\frac{36!}{(36-33)!33!} \\  & =\frac{36!}{3!33!} \\  & =\frac{36\cdot 35\cdot 34\cdot \cancel{33!}}{3!\cdot \cancel{33!}} \\  & =\frac{36\cdot 35\cdot 34}{3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{42\,840}{6} \\  & =7\,140.\end{aligned}
$$
